note: Every number in params is {v, src, note}. src is measured (a data sheet, the firmware or a bench recording) or assumed (a stand-in until a bench recording fits it: scripts/virtual-unit/physics/calibrate.py). Units: meters, kilograms, seconds, newton meters, degrees for angles in this file.
frame: x forward, y left, z up, origin on the yaw axis at table height (the model's Z forward, X left, Y up)

base_w.note: model params (official structure files): base width

base_h.note: model params: table to the top of the turntable ring

base_center_x.note: model params: the turntable sits 4 mm behind the base footprint center

yaw_axis_z.note: model params: yaw joint origin height above the table

neck_w.note: servo holder width, from the model's neck mesh size

pitch_axis_z.note: model params: servo stub height, equal to the head vertical center

head_d.note: model params: published depth with the controller (shell 46.7 mm plus 14.8 mm)

head_center_x.note: model params: the head front is 33.25 mm ahead of the pitch axis, the head is 61.5 mm deep

total_h.note: model params: 70.5 mm published, 70.41 in the files

mass_total.note: maker data sheet, whole robot (187.2 g); the model keeps the same figure

mass_head.note: model params split of the measured total

mass_neck.note: model params split of the measured total

mass_base.note: model params split of the measured total

yaw_range_deg.note: firmware servo init (hal_servo.cpp angleLimit), as the model params record

joints.name: yaw
joints.positive: the head turns clockwise seen from above (the tool's yaw sign)

sensors.name: imu
sensors.note: accelerometer and gyro at the head center in the head frame; tilt is the angle of the body's up axis from gravity

derived.rule: the accelerometer norm leaves 9.81 by more than 2.5 for 150 ms (on), calm again for 1 s (off): the same debounce as the movement limiter (patch ML01)
tilt_deg bands: upright under 15, tilted 15 to 45, side or inverted over 45, with the limiter's hysteresis

before_servo_fix.note: bench window 7 (self.bench.servo_rate): the unit's servo animation ran at 26 to 31 steps a second instead of the designed 50, in every condition (idle, face animating, speaking), so this fit describes the slow behavior. Firmware will fix the animation to real time; record again then and fit as after_servo_fix. Reach was 93 to 96 percent of each step.
